sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: NPC (Neutral-Point Clamped) is a three-level inverter with four switches per leg. The dq-frame current controller decouples the d and q axes. An outer voltage loop regulates the DC bus. The neutral-point voltage must be actively balanced.

sections.heading: Neutral-point balancing
sections.text: The split DC-bus capacitors develop a voltage imbalance due to asymmetric switching. A balancing algorithm adjusts the dwell time of the inner voltage level (zero vector) to equalize the capacitor voltages. The balancing loop bandwidth should be ~1/10 of the current loop.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: Output voltage levels: +V_dc/2, 0, -V_dc/2. Line-to-line voltage has 5 levels. THD is lower than two-level for the same switching frequency. Current-loop crossover: fsw/10. Voltage-loop crossover: fsw/50 to fsw/100. LCL filter resonance: f_res between 10*f_grid and fsw/2.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: NPC requires careful dead-time management to avoid shoot-through and ensure proper zero-level clamping. The inner switches (S2, S3) have different switching loss profiles than the outer switches (S1, S4). Neutral-point balancing fails if the current unbalance exceeds the capacitor sizing margin.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If neutral-point balancing oscillates, reduce the balancing loop gain or increase the DC bus capacitor size. If THD fails spec, check LCL filter resonance placement and active damping. For higher voltage (>1kV), consider T-type or cascaded H-bridge.
